query_text: where does the sound come from when you crack your knuckles

messages.content: where does the sound come from when you crack your knuckles

message.content:
The sound from cracking your knuckles comes from **gas bubbles in the joint fluid**. When you pull the joint apart, pressure drops and bubbles form or change shape; the latest research suggests the noise is produced by the **partial collapse of those bubbles** in the synovial fluid.[1][2][3]

A few details help explain it:

- Your joints contain **synovial fluid**, which lubricates the joint.[1][6]
- Cracking stretches the joint and lowers pressure inside it, letting dissolved gases come out of solution and form bubbles.[1][3]
- Those bubbles are then thought to make the popping sound when they **collapse or partially collapse**.[1][2][3]

There has been some debate over the exact mechanism: older explanations said the sound came from full bubble collapse, while a 2015 study suggested the bubbles persist after cracking, and newer modeling supports **partial collapse** as the sound source.[1][2][3]
